title: Conformal Risk Control
authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Stephen Bates, Adam Fisch, Lihua Lei, Tal Schuster
problem: Conformal prediction bounds one error: a set that misses the true label. Many tasks pay a graded loss instead, such as the fraction of a tumour a mask misses.
idea: Index the outputs by λ: a larger λ gives a more conservative output and never a larger loss.
Choose λ on calibration data so the risk stays at most α even if the next loss is the worst case.

figure.caption: Fig. 1, bottom left: the false-negative rate of the polyp masks over 1000 random splits; α = 0.1 dashed.

takeaway: Take the most liberal threshold whose calibration risk, padded by one worst-case loss, stays at most α: the expected loss on a new point is then at most α.
finding: Expected-loss bound for any bounded monotone loss
method: Loss: any bounded function of the output that never grows as λ grows, e.g. the fraction of a tumour missed.
With a 0/1 miss-the-label loss it is split conformal prediction (§2.3).

formula.reads: The smallest λ whose padded calibration loss is at most α.

measures: Risk: the mean loss on held-out points, per random split.
Set size: what the guarantee costs in pixels, labels or answers.

certifies.event: the expected loss on a new test point
certifies.guarantee: in expectation, not with high probability
certifies.level: α = 0.1, n = 1000 (polyps); losses at most B = 1
certifies.assumes: exchangeable data; loss monotone and right-continuous in λ
certifies.quote: Theorem 1. Assume that Li(λ) is non-increasing in λ, right-continuous

results.text: Polyps, false-negative rate at α = 0.1: mean 0.0987 over 1000 splits.
results.quote: We report results with α = 0.1 in Figure 1. The mean and standard deviation of the risk over 1000 trials are 0.0987 and 0.0114

results.text: ImageNet, graph-distance loss at α = 0.05: mean 0.0499.
results.quote: We report results with α = 0.05 in Figure 3. The mean and standard deviation of the risk over 1000 trials are 0.0499

limits: A loss that is not monotone in λ voids it (Prop. 1).
for_us: With a 0/1 wrong-grasp loss this rule is split conformal prediction; it adds value once errors are graded, an irreversible one costing more.
notes: n = 1000 calibration points for polyps (p.6); every loss in §3 is bounded by 1 (p.5). Theorem 2 (p.4): with i.i.d. losses and no jumps, the risk is at least α − 2B/(n+1). Distribution shift, quantile and multiple risks: §4. Proposition 1 (p.5): for a non-monotone loss the risk can come within any ε of B.
